root_cause.text: In `net/rds/message.c`, `rds_message_purge()` incorrectly determined zerocopy ownership from `rm->m_rs` instead of `data.op_mmp_znotifier`, so an early-failed zerocopy send that had pinned user pages but was not yet queued on a socket was cleaned up with the wrong lifetime/accounting path.
root_cause.evidence: The patch notes “The purge path currently infers zerocopy state from rm->m_rs, so an unqueued message can be cleaned up as if it owned normal payload pages,” and fixes it by capturing `rm->data.op_mmp_znotifier` up front, using it as the discriminator, and adding an `else if (znotifier)` path to call `mm_unaccount_pinned_pages()` and free the notifier when `rm->m_rs` is NULL.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix zerocopy message purge to correctly clean up and free znotifier state even when no socket is attached.
intent_record.what: In rds_message_purge(), a local znotifier pointer was introduced and initialized from rm->data.op_mmp_znotifier under rm->m_rs_lock, then rm->data.op_mmp_znotifier is cleared immediately. The code now uses that saved pointer for the zerocopy callback, and adds a new else-if path for the case where rm->m_rs is NULL but a znotifier still exists: it unaccounts pinned pages via mm_unaccount_pinned_pages() and frees the notifier info with kfree(rds_info_from_znotifier()). The previous inline zcopy flag handling and direct use of rm->data.op_mmp_znotifier inside the rm->m_rs branch were replaced accordingly.
intent_record.how: This change preserves the zerocopy completion notification even if the message no longer has an associated socket lock state, and it prevents the znotifier from being lost when purge runs before the message is queued on a socket. Runtime behavior now correctly releases pinned pages and notifier memory in the no-socket case, avoiding a resource leak and ensuring zerocopy cleanup happens regardless of whether rm->m_rs is still set.

relevance_review.reason: The group’s intent matches the root cause: it fixes rds_message_purge() zerocopy cleanup to use the correct znotifier state when no socket is attached, addressing the wrong lifetime/accounting path for early-failed zerocopy sends.

candidates.rationale: This condition makes zerocopy cleanup depend on whether a socket is attached, which is the wrong lifetime signal for an early-failed zerocopy send. The vulnerable path could have pinned pages and a znotifier without any socket association yet.

This is the actual zerocopy cleanup guard in the pre-fix code, but the root cause says ownership was determined from rm->m_rs instead of the znotifier state. Its execution was incorrectly gated by the surrounding socket check.
The purge path assumes a valid socket object and derives cleanup/accounting from it, which is incorrect for messages that failed before being queued on a socket.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the incorrect ownership/lifetime gate in rds_message_purge(): zerocopy cleanup was made dependent on socket attachment rather than on the znotifier state, so early-failed zerocopy sends with pinned pages but no socket were handled on the wrong path.

This statement ties purge/accounting to rm->m_rs, which is the root mistake described: the code inferred zerocopy ownership from the socket pointer instead of from data.op_mmp_znotifier, causing incorrect cleanup for messages not yet queued on a socket.
